ruling.recommended_action: Close the case with no refund; no account action. The 09:20–09:26 segment is covered by the rider's own pre-segment general route authorisation, so the $45.04 metered fare stands.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a completed RydeTAXI metered trip; there is one off-route segment, 09:20–09:26, 4.04 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.86 km, +2.18 km [F3], against an overall 21.6 km vs 19.3 km optimal [F1] and a $45.04 metered total [F7]. RD-1 is therefore engaged and the segment must be tested segment-by-segment under RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5 [F3][RD-1][RD-2].

RD-4 gives the driver nothing: the trace marks ✗ no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch [F3][RD-4], and F15 confirms no traffic incident near the route in the trip window. The only congestion reading is EAST COAST PARKWAY band 2 (10–19 km/h, 08:58–09:20) [F12], which under RD-4(b) is corroborative only and cannot exempt a segment on its own; AIRPORT BOULEVARD band 5 and OPHIR ROAD band 4 [F13][F14] plus fair weather [F16] show no severe congestion. So no exemption flows from RD-4 [F12][F15][RD-4].

The decisive question is RD-5 consent scope. The driver's message at 09:17 [F8] asked whether to take another way; the rider's own message at 09:18 [F9] — sent before the segment started at 09:20 [F3][F10] — answered "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late." That is on its face a general route choice: it names no road, imposes no condition, and leaves the alternative route to the driver [F9][F3][RD-5]. Both advocates state the same ground for F3 — general_route_consent — and that stipulation binds me [F8][F9][RD-5]. The rider's submission that a general authority does not reach a 1027 m stray is a pure corridor-distance argument; F3's metres-from-corridor figure is not a policy criterion under RD-5, and the record shows no stop of the driver's own, no errand, and no loop that failed to reach the destination — the car ended at Changi T3 [F7][F3][RD-5]. The record is a complete, fully timestamped chat of 2 messages [F10], so there is no G12 incompleteness, and F11 is the driver's post-trip statement, which under G11 is not itself consent and is not relied on [F11][RD-5]. On the words as written, the pre-segment agreement covers the route chosen to reach the destination, and the segment is exempt [F9][F3][RD-5].

Because the only segment is exempt, the sum of extra_km of non-exempt segments is 0.00 km, and 0.00 km × $1.4102/km = $0.00 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The billed excess of $3.31 on 2.35 km at $1.4102/km (this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km) [F4] includes the portion of the actual 2.3 km excess inside the optimal-route corridor, which RD-2 does not refund in any event [F1][F7][RD-2]. The 0.4-min metered waiting charge of $0.11 [F5] is a metered waiting unit on a RydeTAXI trip, expressly non-refundable under RD-3(c) [RD-3], and the breakdown contains only published items with no surge [F6][F7][FARE-1]. RD-6 does not bite: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 for this driver [F18], so no account flag arises [F18][RD-6]. The result is no_action with no amount [F3][RD-2].

I record the reservation that the rider's reading — that "whichever way is faster" does not license a 2.18 km addition that made the trip 35.4 min against a 25.2 min estimate [F2] — is not frivolous; but the trace settles the RD-4 screen and the scope of a general-authority message is a reading of the words, which the record as it stands supports as covering the route to the destination [F2][F9][RD-5].

segment_findings.reason: Driver asked at 09:17 whether to take another way [F8]; the rider's own message at 09:18 said 'Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late' [F9], sent before the segment started at 09:20 and fully timestamped [F3][F10]. That is a general route choice covering the route chosen to reach Changi T3, not an errand or a stop of the driver's own, and no road was named so no named-road limitation applies [F8][F9][F3][RD-5]. Both advocates stipulate this ground [RD-5].

rejected_claims.reason: The off-route segment and the +2.3 km overall are correctly recorded [F1][F3] and RD-1 is engaged, but the claim that the deviation is unexplained fails: the rider's own pre-segment message [F9] authorises the route choice and the segment is exempt under RD-5 [F3][F9][RD-5].

Accepted as a reading of the exchange [F8][F9], but it supports the driver: a general route choice covers the route chosen to reach the destination, and the car reached Changi T3 [F7], so the segment does not count [F9][F3][RD-5].

The timing of consent is conceded and consent being pre-segment satisfies RD-5's 'before you go' [F9][F3][F10]; the residual point — that 1027 m from the optimal route exceeds a general authority — relies on a corridor-distance measure that is not a policy criterion, and no driver's errand or stop appears in the record [F3][F9][RD-5].

Correct and uncontested: F11 is the driver's post-trip statement and adds nothing to consent [F11][RD-5]; the driver expressly rests on F9 alone, so this point does not change the outcome [F11][F9][RD-5].

Correct that RD-4 does not exempt (no incident on the replaced stretch) [F12][F15][RD-4], but RD-4 and RD-5 are independent routes of exemption; the failure of RD-4 leaves the RD-5 consent exemption standing [F8][F9][RD-4][RD-5].

The arithmetic (2.18 km of extra_km on the segment, at the fare record's $1.4102/km) is right [F3][F4], but the premise that the segment is unexempted is wrong: with the segment exempt the sum of non-exempt extra_km is 0.00 km and $0.00 is refundable [F3][F4][RD-2].

Accepted: the $0.11 waiting item is a metered waiting unit [F5], non-refundable on RydeTAXI under RD-3(c), and the breakdown otherwise contains only published items with no surge [F6][F7][FARE-1]; the rider's own concession in this claim removes any fee dispute [F5][RD-3].
RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 and F18 records route: 0 for this driver, and no refund arises, so no account flag is warranted [F18][F4][RD-6].

The 'reasonable cause' framing is not adopted: F12 is a speed band, which under RD-4(b) cannot exempt by itself, and the trace marks the RD-4(a) incident screen ✗ [F12][F3][RD-4]; the driver's outcome nevertheless follows from RD-5 consent [F8][F9][RD-5].
